title: Khoshut Khanate
capsule: The Khoshut Khanate was founded by Güshi Khan of the Oirat Khoshut tribe, who invaded Tibet between 1637 and 1642, defeated the rival Tsangpa Khan, and established Gelug supremacy by granting the Fifth Dalai Lama Ngawang Lobsang Gyatso temporal authority over Tibet while retaining military paramountcy himself. Güshi Khan died in 1655; his successors exercised declining effective control as Tibetan regents and the Dalai Lama institution accrued increasing administrative power. Lhazang Khan (r. 1697–1717) attempted to reassert Khoshut dominance by deposing and killing Regent Sangye Gyatso in 1705 and installing a compliant sixth Dalai Lama candidate, but was killed in 1717 when Dzungar Mongol forces under Tsewang Rabtan invaded and occupied Lhasa.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Khoshut territorial control over the Tibetan plateau is attested in Tibetan and Chinese Qing sources, though the precise extent of effective versus nominal suzerainty outside central Tibet is difficult to delineate.
